prompt:
gen/build_reports.py reads an order export (default input/orders.csv) and writes four report files into an output folder (default out/). On this Windows machine it produces wrong files, and it fails on some input. Fix the script so that `python gen/build_reports.py` (and with --input PATH and --out DIR, where DIR may not exist yet and may already exist) writes exactly the output described here.

Input: input/orders.csv has the columns id, customer, amount, status. It uses CRLF line endings. Another export may use LF, may have empty lines, and may have spaces around the id, customer and status values. Amounts can be written with thousands separators inside quotes ("1,250.00"), with no decimals (5), or with more than two decimals (2.675). No CR character may ever reach an output file.

Output rules for all four files:
1. Every line ends with LF, never CRLF, on every platform.
2. Each file ends with exactly one newline: no missing newline and no empty last line.
3. Each file is UTF-8 without a BOM, and non ASCII characters are written as they are (also in the JSON file, never as \uXXXX escapes).
4. Orders are sorted by the number after the last hyphen of the id, as a number (A-9 before A-10 before A-100), and then by the whole id.
5. Amounts are parsed as decimal numbers from the text (remove the thousands separators), rounded half up to two decimals, and always printed with a dot and exactly two decimals (5 becomes 5.00, 2.675 becomes 2.68). Totals are the sum of the rounded amounts.
6. A status is trimmed and lower cased ("PAID " becomes paid). Orders whose status is cancelled are left out of summary.txt, by_customer.json and report.md, but they stay in orders.tsv.

For the supplied input/orders.csv the four files must be byte for byte these (\t is a tab character):

summary.txt
```
orders: 5
customers: 3
total: 1623.15
largest: A-9 (1250.00)
```

orders.tsv
```
id\tcustomer\tamount\tstatus
A-9\tAlan Wu\t1250.00\tpaid
A-10\tŁukasz Nowak\t310.50\tpaid
A-11\tAlan Wu\t0.75\tshipped
A-12\tZoë Martin\t19.90\tpaid
A-100\tŁukasz Nowak\t42.00\tpaid
A-101\tZoë Martin\t5.00\tcancelled
```

by_customer.json (2 space indentation, keys sorted, each total is a string with two decimals)
```
{
  "Alan Wu": {
    "orders": 2,
    "total": "1250.75"
  },
  "Zoë Martin": {
    "orders": 1,
    "total": "19.90"
  },
  "Łukasz Nowak": {
    "orders": 2,
    "total": "352.50"
  }
}
```

report.md
```
# Order report

| id | customer | amount |
|---|---|---|
| A-9 | Alan Wu | 1250.00 |
| A-10 | Łukasz Nowak | 310.50 |
| A-11 | Alan Wu | 0.75 |
| A-12 | Zoë Martin | 19.90 |
| A-100 | Łukasz Nowak | 42.00 |

Total: 1623.15
```

In summary.txt, customers is the number of different customer names among the orders that are not cancelled, and largest is the id and amount of the order with the highest amount among them (the lower id wins a tie). The script is also checked on other input files, so do not hard code these values. Check the bytes of your output files, for example with `od -c` or Python in binary mode, not only what the terminal shows.
